messages:
jordan: Quick async standup: what I did / blockers / today
jordan: Did the routepolicy rollout to staging, saw ~3% 429 increase on the token-bucket routes.
maya: Thanks — saw that in SLO dashboard, digging into traces now :mag:
ryan: Can you paste the curl that reproduces 429? want to test locally.
jordan: Sure, here — reproduces after ~120 req/s per instance
```
curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/encode -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"input":"test"}' -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"
for i in seq 1 200; do curl ...; done
```
maya: Re: traces, looks like one pod started rejecting due to token-bucket overflow, upstream had reduced burst-size in config.
ryan: Which config? route-level? global?
jordan: Route-level policy in `configs/route-policies.yaml` — snippet:
```
- route: /v1/encode
  rate_limit:
    unit: second
    requests: 100
    burst: 50
```
maya: @sasha can you review the PR to increase burst to 150 for staging? PR is #2147.
sasha: On it, will skim now. Quick Q: do we have metrics for kv-cache hit ratio tied to rate bursts?
jordan: Not directly, but cache hits drop when backpressure causes queuing. I can add a tag on requests for correlation today.
deploy-bot: Can confirm: canary deployment to staging completed at 1713456800, traffic split 10% -> config v2
ryan: If PR approved, let's run a 10-minute soak with loadgen to validate.
maya: Blocker: need approvals for terraform change to bump pod CPU on staging to handle extra burst.
sasha: Reviewing PR, adding a small note about testing and rollback plan :thumbsup: 
jordan: Thanks — I'll open the terraform PR and tag infra. Plan: PR -> canary soak -> monitor 5xx/429 for 30m -> promote.
maya: Today I'll follow traces, correlate with cache hits and open an item in ops board if needed.
ryan: I'll run the loadgen after infra green.
sasha: LGTM pending test results.
jordan: pinging @sasha in ~30m for final approval. If anything blocks, call me.
